name: Funneling and focusing questions
summary: 2,348 exchanges from 4th and 5th grade math lessons, a student's turn and the teacher's reply, each labelled by three raters as a funneling question, a focusing question or neither.

license.note: The repository's LICENSE is MIT, and the repository holds the data. Its exchanges are excerpts of the anonymized NCTE transcripts, which as a whole are for research only (ncte-transcripts).

cite: Alic, S., Demszky, D., Mancenido, Z., Liu, J., Hill, H., & Jurafsky, D. (2022). Computationally Identifying Funneling and Focusing Questions in Classroom Discourse. BEA 2022, 224-233. https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2022.bea-1.27

fits.how: Raters' labels to check a judge model that rates whether a tutor's question asks the learner to reflect on their own thinking or funnels them toward an answer, a move a tutor that gives hints has to get right.

connect.note: Checks your judge model against raters, with no labels of your own: a teacher's reply most of three raters called a focusing question should pass, and a funneling one should fail, half each; neither is left out. It describes your judge on classroom talk and this rubric, not your agent. The students are children, anonymized: running it sends their words to the model you name. Never try to identify a student or a teacher.
